description: A black-and-white collie lies flat on the plank floor exactly where it can see both pens at once, small at the far end of the frame, chin on its paws, plainly on duty.
A tabby barn cat is stretched out small along the top of the bale stack above the pens, one paw hanging over the edge, watching the whole business without comment.
A robin sits small on the top rail of a hurdle at the edge of the frame, head cocked, waiting for the next drift of wool to be swept over.
A speckled hen has walked in and is settled small in the loose wool at the back of the shed, wings spread flat, taking a dust bath in somebody else's day's work.
Two swallows turn small under the rafters at the far end, in and out through the open gable, entirely untroubled by the racket below them.
A young collie sits small and bolt upright just inside the door, tail going hard, plainly desperate to be allowed in and plainly not allowed in.
A ginger cat is curled small in a wooden crate of wool at the wall, only its back showing above the rim, having decided this is now a cat bed.
A grey terrier stands small on the swept floor with one front foot raised, a fat tuft of loose wool in its mouth, looking for somewhere better to put it.
A brown hen roosts small on the top bar of a hurdle at the back of the shed, looking down over the pens with open disapproval.
A collie lies small and flat on the flags beside the yard gate with its chin on its paws, one eye open, holding the whole race on its own.
A brown goat has its head small over the top of the yard gate, chewing, watching the pens with the close attention of a neighbour who was not invited.
Three white ducks have come up small along the wall line in a loose untidy huddle, entirely off course and going wherever this turns out to lead.
A tortoiseshell cat sits small on the top of the stone wall behind the pens, tail curled round its feet, supervising from the safest place in the yard.
Two pigeons walk small along the ridge of the shed gable above the pens, back and forth, going nowhere with enormous purpose.
A tan pony stands small at the far corner of the yard with its head over the rail, plainly convinced the whole event has been staged for its benefit.
A wagtail runs small across the packed earth of the gateway in quick stops and starts, tail going, picking over the wool the flock has left behind it.
